newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crudes fall with WTI Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crudes fall with WTI Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell Tuesday, tracking a late day fall in futures and spot crudes after weekly inventory data showed most nationwide petroleum stocks rose, traders said.
Trade turned quiet Tuesday after last week's active market, which saw Exxon sell two full cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at sharply lower discounts.
ANS traded for $1.50 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude, the U.S. benchmark grade.
In response to lower prices, BP, the biggest producer of ANS, lowered its offer 15 cents a barrel Monday to $1.30 under WTI.
Trade also turned quiet as traders left for an industry function.
Tuesday's flat discounts and 30-cent drop on WTI sent outright ANS ANS prices down 30 cents, to $21.05/21.15 a barrel.
Kern River crude prices rose with Monday's rise in postings, to $14.31/14.41 a barrel.
Wilmington and Line 63 markets remained idle.
